title: Due status vs work order status; Invoice or Mark complete clears a row
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in, on the build under test, as a service advisor with the view customers and create and edit customers permissions. Raising a work order also needs create and edit work orders.
  2. Open Customers from the top navigation and switch to its "Maintenance reminders" tab.
  3. Rows that are due soon, due today and overdue, and one not yet due (seed with last service dates at enrolment).
  4. From some rows create work orders (Create work order) and take them to: Estimate; Approved; declined; Complete (finish the lines and complete the work order without invoicing). Keep two Complete-not-invoiced rows.
custom_steps:
1. Read the column headed "Due status" for each row, including the not-yet-due one.
  2. Compare a row's due-status badge with the badge beside its work order number.
  3. Read the Work Order column for a row with no work order, one with a live work order, and the declined one.
  4. Read the work order badges you created (Estimate, Approved, Complete) and look for "On Hold" anywhere.
  5. On the first Complete row press Invoice and invoice the work order; return to the list.
  6. On the second Complete row open the three-dot menu > Mark complete, keep the default Reset date and confirm.
  7. Hover the (i) on the due-status column heading and note the heading the build shows.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The due-status column carries only due soon, due today and overdue, and is empty for the not-yet-due row.
  • The work order status appears only as the badge beside the work order number; it is never shown in the due-status column.
  • No work order: a dash. Live work order: a link with its status badge, and the button reads Open work order. Declined: still linked with its badge, and the row offers Create work order again.
  • Each badge shows the work order's status as the app names it (e.g. Estimate, Approved, Complete); "On Hold" never appears.
  • Invoice opens that work order's invoicing; once invoiced, the service resets and the row leaves the list.
  • Mark complete resets the service at once and the row leaves the list without waiting for an invoice.
  • On the design the (i) reads "Overdue: past its due date. Due today: an exact certificate or calendar date that falls today. Due soon: inside the first reminder, 14 days by default. Empty: not yet due." (the design heads the column "Status"; the spec says "Due status": record the build's heading).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780, story SV-10570 (S13, The maintenance reminders worklist), Chunk 1 MR (Confluence 886931488) as edited 5 October 2026, S13 (S13-R13, S13-R14, S13-R23, S13-R25, S13-R26); Design board "Chunk 1.dc.html" (MR V2 Claude Design project, version of 6 October 2026), artboard S1 (Status column); read 6 Oct 2026.
